    23	Overview
    24	---------
    25	
    26	LMfit-py provides a Least-Squares Minimization routine and class with a simple,
    27	flexible approach to parameterizing a model for fitting to data.
    28	
    29	LMfit is a pure Python package, and so easy to install from source or with
    30	``pip install lmfit``.
    31	
    32	For questions, comments, and suggestions, please use the `LMfit mailing list`_.
    33	Using the bug tracking software in GitHub Issues is encouraged for known
    34	problems and bug reports. Please read
    35	`Contributing.md <.github/CONTRIBUTING.md>`_ before creating an Issue.
    36	
    37	
    38	Parameters and Fitting
    39	-------------------------
    40	
    41	LMfit-py provides a Least-Squares Minimization routine and class with a simple,
    42	flexible approach to parameterizing a model for fitting to data. Named
    43	Parameters can be held fixed or freely adjusted in the fit, or held between
    44	lower and upper bounds. In addition, parameters can be constrained as a simple
    45	mathematical expression of other Parameters.
    46	
    47	To do this, the programmer defines a Parameters object, an enhanced dictionary,
    48	containing named parameters::
    49	
    50	    fit_params = Parameters()
    51	    fit_params['amp'] = Parameter(value=1.2, min=0.1, max=1000)
    52	    fit_params['cen'] = Parameter(value=40.0, vary=False)
    53	    fit_params['wid'] = Parameter(value=4, min=0)
    54	
    55	or using the equivalent::
    56	
    57	    fit_params = Parameters()
    58	    fit_params.add('amp', value=1.2, min=0.1, max=1000)
    59	    fit_params.add('cen', value=40.0, vary=False)
    60	    fit_params.add('wid', value=4, min=0)
    61	
    62	The programmer will also write a function to be minimized (in the least-squares
    63	sense) with its first argument being this Parameters object, and additional
    64	positional and keyword arguments as desired::
    65	
    66	    def myfunc(params, x, data, someflag=True):
    67	        amp = params['amp'].value
    68	        cen = params['cen'].value
    69	        wid = params['wid'].value
    70	        ...
    71	        return residual_array
    72	
    73	For each call of this function, the values for the params may have changed,
    74	subject to the bounds and constraint settings for each Parameter. The function
    75	should return the residual (i.e., data-model) array to be minimized.
    76	
    77	The advantage here is that the function to be minimized does not have to be
    78	changed if different bounds or constraints are placed on the fitting Parameters.
    79	The fitting model (as described in myfunc) is instead written in terms of
    80	physical parameters of the system, and remains remains independent of what is
    81	actually varied in the fit. In addition, which parameters are adjusted and which
    82	are fixed happens at run-time, so that changing what is varied and what
    83	constraints are placed on the parameters can easily be modified by the user in
    84	real-time data analysis.
    85	
    86	To perform the fit, the user calls::
    87	
    88	    result = minimize(myfunc, fit_params, args=(x, data), kws={'someflag':True}, ....)
    89	
    90	After the fit, a ``MinimizerResult`` class is returned that holds the results
    91	the fit (e.g., fitting statistics and optimized parameters). The dictionary
    92	``result.params`` contains the best-fit values, estimated standard deviations,
    93	and correlations with other variables in the fit.
    94	
    95	By default, the underlying fit algorithm is the Levenberg-Marquart algorithm
    96	with numerically-calculated derivatives from MINPACK's lmdif function, as used
    97	by ``scipy.optimize.leastsq``. Most other solvers that are present in ``scipy``
    98	(e.g., Nelder-Mead, differential_evolution, basinhopping, etctera) are also
    99	supported.
